hub.speaker: Lupe
hub.text: Cans, caps, and good gossip. What do you need?

lore.speaker: Lupe
lore.text: Buff Kings are pressed — word is some new writer's been taking VEK's walls. Chrome Saints move through the train yard after dark, and the city's cleanup crew got fresh budget this month. Don't sleep on your best spots.

hub.speaker: Prime
hub.text: New blood with a can. I've watched writers come and go on this block for thirty years.

choices.lockedText: (Come back when you're Known on this block)

who.speaker: Prime
who.text: Darnell. They wrote PRIME. Every fill you ever bit traces back to somebody — mine traced to the ones before me. That's how style works: it's a lineage, not a costume.

lesson.speaker: Prime
lesson.text: Letters first, style second. Your throwie's E leans lazy — tighten the spine, let the bar swing. Style is a debt you pay forward to the ones who came before.

effects.message: Prime schooled you on letter structure. (+40 rep)

hub.speaker: Vesper
hub.text: Vesper. I scout for the White Walls gallery. Your name is all over two districts — collectors pay for that kind of authentic. Bring me a canvas, freehand, your best work. I judge what it's worth.

choices.lockedText: (Make your name first — come back when you're Known)

choices.text: What does the street think of this?

tension.speaker: Vesper
tension.text: The street says gallery money is selling out. The gallery says the street is free marketing. Your crew will hear about every canvas I sell — that costs you something with them. That's the trade.

hub.speaker: Moth
hub.text: Eyes open. Quiet night so far.

choices.text: Why'd Ghost Line take your book?

watch.speaker: Moth
watch.text: Cameras sweep, guards loop, civilians stare too long. I count the gaps. You paint in the gaps.

book.speaker: Moth
book.text: They said I 'owed' them for painting their alley — took three years of outlines as payment. Now I watch their walls for you instead. Funny how that goes.

hub.speaker: Caps
hub.text: Fat caps, fast hands. Empty walls make a claimed block look nervous.

choices.text: What do you do for the crew?

role.speaker: Caps
role.text: You take the block, I make sure it looks taken. Throwies on the weak spots, no speeches.

hub.speaker: Metro
hub.text: I listen to routes. Security talks before they move.

role.speaker: Metro
role.text: One clean pull per heat level. After that, they learn the route and you're on your own until the block cools or spikes.

hub.speaker: Indigo
hub.text: Indigo. Printmaking, second year. I screen posters and cut slaps when I'm not in the studio. Saw your throwies — you'd kill it on paper.

choices.lockedText: (Get your name up first — come back when you're an Up writer)

why.speaker: Indigo
why.text: Cans get you nicked. A slap goes up in two seconds, a wheatpaste in twenty — flat, quiet, and it sticks to glass, doors, poles, anything a fill won't bite. They buff easy, sure, but you can paper a whole block before anyone smells the glue.

choices.lockedText: (Get your name up first — come back when you're an Up writer)

lesson.speaker: Indigo
lesson.text: Flour, water, a little sugar — cook it down and it's stronger than most glue. Print your name, slap your stickers, paper the spots cans can't reach. Just know the bucket's bulky; carry it and you read suspicious.

effects.message: Indigo taught you to cut slaps and cook wheatpaste. Stickers and posters unlocked. (+20 rep)
